recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Only revisit core source if FHIR-45445 or a later Applied/Published decision explicitly requires moving or expanding the detailed naming-convention rules in the core specification.
issue_request: FHIR-14961 was a Published FHIR-core STU3 change request asking for a consistent convention for multi-word search parameter and modifier names. Its final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution declined disruptive renames and required documentation that search parameter names use sensible casing and must not differ only by case.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites svn revision 13883, which maps to git-svn commit 75cbf026343379dc52cb3143d3f5c373ff73beeb. That commit added the search-page paragraph stating that search parameter names are case sensitive, HL7 does not define parameters that differ only by case, clients should use correct case, and servers must not define different-meaning case-only variants.
additional_context: Current source/search.html still carries the case-collision rule. The active SearchParameter resource in source/fhir.ini also defines SearchParameter.code with compatibility guidance to use lowercase ASCII characters and hyphens, and later FHIR-45349 source work prohibited separator characters. FHIR-45445 is a later, broader Resolved - change required issue for IG-guidance naming rules for new search and operation parameters, not an Applied/Published core source decision in this run.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current core specification already conveys the required FHIR-14961 rule and later source context reinforces the same naming direction without requiring retroactive renames.

related_jiras.note: Later Resolved - change required issue for broader naming-convention guidance in IG-guidance and new parameters; not final Applied/Published core-source work for this run.
